answer: Admission opens with a memory-bus latency probe: the verifier allocates a contiguous 8 GB shale-like region on the candidate node and measures first-touch access against a nanosecond budget, issuing a velvet sequence of cache-line reads whose timing must stay under 40 ns per hop. A genuine identity answers from local silicon; a Sybil spinning thousands of keys on one host cannot, because its shared bus saturates and a whisper of jitter (past 90 ns) trips the audit.
